questions.question: You are driving a passenger car towing a small caravan with a total combined mass of 3.5 tonnes. You approach an intersection where the combination sign shown above is displayed. What are you legally allowed to do?

options.text: You are strictly prohibited from turning left because the restriction applies to all vehicles towing trailers or caravans.
You may turn left because the prohibition applies only to goods vehicles with a gross vehicle mass (GVM) exceeding 10 tonnes.
You must turn left immediately because this sign indicates a compulsory lane diversion for all light vehicles.
You cannot turn left, and you must come to a complete stop to allow oncoming heavy vehicles to pass you.

questions.explanation: The no-left-turn sign with a '10 t' goods-vehicle plate applies only to goods vehicles with a GVM over 10 tonnes; a car towing a 3.5 t caravan may turn left.

questions.question: Which statement regarding the use of a vehicle's hooter is correct?

options.text: It may be used to greet another driver provided it is brief
It may be used whenever a driver believes it will improve traffic flow
It may only be used when necessary in the interests of safety
It may be used to signal impatience to a slower vehicle

questions.explanation: A hooter may only be used when necessary for safety reasons, not to greet or show impatience.

questions.question: You are driving a standard private passenger car and notice a commercial vehicle parked on the side of the road directly behind the sign combination provided. Under what circumstances applies the restriction shown on this sign?

options.text: No vehicle of any kind is permitted to stop on this section of the road at any time.
Only vehicles carrying dangerous goods are strictly prohibited from stopping here.
Turning or reversing is prohibited for all vehicles transporting hazardous chemical substances.
Heavy cargo trucks are prohibited from parking overnight, but light delivery vehicles may stop.

questions.explanation: The no-stopping sign combined with the dangerous-goods plate means the prohibition applies only to vehicles carrying dangerous goods.

questions.question: A private motor vehicle is fitted with a siren that plays a musical tune. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It is legal provided the volume is below the hooter volume
It is legal if used only on private property
It is legal if the driver has held a licence for more than 5 years
Such warning devices that play a tune may not be used on private vehicles

questions.explanation: Sirens or warning devices that play a tune may not be fitted to or used on private vehicles.

questions.question: You approach an intersection and a traffic officer is standing directly ahead of you displaying the hand signal shown. Which traffic flow is legally required to stop?

options.text: Only traffic approaching the officer from behind must come to a complete stop.
All traffic approaching the officer from both the front and behind must stop simultaneously.
Only traffic approaching the officer from the front must stop.
All traffic inside the intersection must clear it immediately, but no new vehicles need to stop.

questions.explanation: An officer facing you with one arm raised vertically: traffic approaching from the front must stop.

questions.question: A child is 13 years old and 1.6 metres tall. For seatbelt purposes, how is that person classified?

options.text: As a child because they are under 14 years old
As an adult because they are taller than 1.5 metres
As a child until they reach 14 years old
Classification depends on whether they sit in the front or rear seat

questions.explanation: For seatbelt purposes a person taller than 1.5 m is treated as an adult regardless of age.

questions.question: You approach an intersection from behind a traffic officer who is standing as shown. What does this signal legally require you to do?

options.text: You may proceed straight through the intersection without slowing down, as the signal is only intended for cross-traffic.
You must bring your vehicle to a complete stop before entering the intersection.
You are permitted to turn left immediately, but you cannot proceed straight or turn right.
You must drive past the officer on their left side only, ensuring you yield to oncoming pedestrians.

questions.explanation: Approaching an officer from behind while the officer's arm is extended sideways: you must stop before the intersection.

questions.question: Under which circumstance is wearing a seatbelt NOT compulsory?

options.text: When travelling below 20 km/h
While reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay
When seated in the rear of the vehicle
While travelling on a private road

questions.explanation: Wearing a seatbelt is not compulsory while reversing or moving into or out of a parking bay.

questions.question: You approach an intersection driving a vehicle from the front of the traffic officer who is standing as shown. Which traffic stream must come to a stop?

options.text: Only traffic approaching the officer from the rear must stop.
Only traffic approaching the officer from the side of the lowered arm must stop.
Traffic approaching the officer from both the front and the rear must stop.
Traffic approaching from the right side may proceed, while all other streams must stop.

questions.explanation: With one arm raised and the other extended, traffic approaching from both the front and the rear must stop.

questions.question: A driver is approaching a vehicle displaying a red warning light and sounding a siren. What is the correct action?

options.text: Continue driving normally if the vehicle is in another lane
Give immediate right of way to the emergency vehicle
Only yield if the emergency vehicle is approaching from behind
Stop immediately in the roadway regardless of circumstances

questions.explanation: Give immediate right of way to an emergency vehicle displaying a red light and sounding a siren.
